title: Did small-brained Homo naledi bury its dead?
summary: Excavators claimed burials and engravings at Rising Star Cave, but the burial claims caused significant academic backlash and many paleontologists question the engravings.
why: If true, symbolic burial would not require a big brain, upending ideas of what makes humans unique.
question: Did Homo naledi deliberately bury its dead and engrave cave walls?
evidence: Fossils dated about 335,000–236,000 years ago (2017); burial claims criticised on taphonomic, stratigraphic and mineralogical grounds.
wouldSettle: Independent excavation and sediment analysis showing deliberately dug pits, and secure dating of the engravings.

theories.name: Deliberate burial
theories.idea: Excavators argue Homo naledi intentionally placed bodies in dug graves.

theories.name: Natural accumulation
theories.idea: Critics question the taphonomic and stratigraphic evidence that the bodies were buried on purpose.
